question_text: An Indigenous Cultural Community (ICC) in Mindanao claims ancestral domain over a tract of land that a mining company has been granted a permit to explore. Under RA 8371 (Indigenous Peoples Rights Act or IPRA), which of the following is the most accurate statement regarding the ICC's rights?

options.text: The ICC has no right to the land because the mining permit was issued by the government.

The ICC has the right to ancestral domain, which includes the right to manage and control the land, and the mining company must secure the ICC's free, prior, and informed consent (FPIC) before any exploration.
The ICC can only claim the land if they have a Torrens title issued by the government.
The ICC's rights are limited to the surface of the land, and the mining company can explore the sub-surface without consent.
